national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 243 Nationwide cleanliness drive being conducted as part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
national_raw_news.content: The nationwide Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath cleanliness drive is being conducted as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign. The objective of the campaign is to ensure cleanliness, improve sanitation and create awareness about hygiene and proper waste disposal among the general public. Several Union Ministers, Chief Minister and senior officials are participating in the cleanliness drive across the country. The Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign, which began on 17th of last month, will be observed till 17th of October. The theme of this year’s campaign is – Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat, which underlines the role of collective participation and shared responsibility in advancing the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. Union Jal Shakti Minister C R Paatil participated in a Shramdaan activity at Kalindi Kunj Ghat in New Delhi. Talking to reporters, Mr Paatil said that cleanliness and water conservation are inseparable and emphasised the need to keep rivers clean. He said that treating rivers as garbage bins and dumping waste into them will pollute the water and adversely affect human life. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju attended the Swachhata Hi Seva programme at Peshwa Road Navyug School in the national capital. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on cleanliness and sanitation. Mr Rijiju said that a cleaner India will lead to a healthier India. Union Minister For Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy also participated in the cleanliness drive in Delhi. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Reddy said, ‘Cleanliness is not just about cleaning, but it should be a part of the behaviour. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi also undertook the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 cleanliness drive at Gargi College in New Delhi. During the drive, he interacted with the students, including from the NSS, NCC and sports communities and appreciated their enthusiasm and active participation. Mr Joshi said that the students’ commitment to cleanliness and civic responsibility was truly encouraging. Union Minister for Civil Aviation Ram Mohan Naidu has said that cleanliness is a continuous process and should become an integral part of our daily work and thinking. Addressing a programme organised at the Ministry of Civil Aviation under the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign, Mr Naidu urged everyone to become ambassadors of cleanliness and contribute towards making India cleaner. He said the government’s aim is to make cleanliness a key pillar of the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. He added that even the smallest contribution can make a significant difference in achieving this goal. The Civil Aviation Minister said that airports across the country are also emerging as symbols of cleanliness. He noted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Swachhata mission is no longer limited to cities but is reaching the grassroots level. Mr Naidu said that everyone is committed to building a clean India.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 407 PM Modi says India’s 21st-century work culture rooted in Pro-People, Pro-Active and Good Go...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the country is moving rapidly on the Reform Express and the institutions that conduct examinations must also work on reforms that are the need of the country. Addressing the Centenary Celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that an examination should not be considered just an event as it is related to the future of the youth. Mr Modi noted that a delay of even a few months can create difficulties for the youth, and therefore, the examination system should follow the principle of time certainty. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that over the 100-year journey of UPSC, the generations, governments, technology, and syllabi have changed, but the trust in this institution remains as unwavering as ever. Mr Modi stressed the need to bring young people into public services who are drawn not to public office but to public service. He said, today, 21st-century India is moving forward with a new work culture and its core principle is Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance. The Prime Minister said his Government’s mantra is Nagarik Devo Bhava and serving the citizens is paramount. He said, for a Viksit Bharat, the kind of governance the country now needs will be enabled to a great extent by institutions such as the UPSC and the State Public Service Commissions. Mr Modi said the young people being recruited today will play an important role in building a Viksit Bharat. Prime Minister Modi said India in 2047 will be very different from the India of today. He said India will be more urban, the gap between villages and cities will be smaller, and the aspirations and expectations of the citizens, especially the youth, will be much higher. He said the next 20 to 25 years will be extremely important for every Indian and for every institution in the country. Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh said that UPSC has achieved several milestones and added many new dimensions during the last twelve years. He said the number of government appointments made through UPSC has increased, and transparency in the recruitment system has also improved, leading to greater public trust. Dr Singh highlighted that approximately 65 thousand appointments were made through the UPSC during the NDA’s 12-year tenure, compared with around 45 thousand appointments during the UPA’s ten-year tenure. The Minister said that today, UPSC has become a role model for recruitment agencies across the country and the world. Chairman UPSC Dr Ajay Kumar said, since independence, generations of the nation’s youth have come to the Commission’s doorstep with dreams of serving the country and UPSC has ensured that they are judged solely on the touchstone of merit. He said, currently, women constitute approximately 30 per cent of the successful candidates in the Civil Services Examination. Dr Kumar said, measures such as identifying duplicate applications with the help of Artificial Intelligence, real-time OCR-based evaluation of millions of documents uploaded by candidates and face authentication for lakhs of candidates at examination centers are some of the recent steps adopted by the Commission to further strengthen fairness and security. The programme marks the culmination of year-long celebrations that commenced on 1st October last year, commemorating 100 years since the establishment of the UPSC in 1926. On the occasion, Prime Minister Modi released a UPSC Centenary Commemorative Coin, a Commemorative Stamp and a Book titled ‘100 Landmark Judgements – Shaping the Policies of UPSC and Public Service Commissions in India ‘.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 126 Govt cuts sugar stock holding period of dealers to 15 days to check hoarding and other malpractices
national_raw_news.content: The Government has reduced the stock holding period for sugar dealers to 15 days and fixed the stock holding limit at one thousand quintals, with effect from the 15th of this month. It will remain effective till November this year. Consumer Affairs Ministry said that the government has revised the sugar stock holding norms to prevent hoarding and ensure smooth supply to consumers during the festive season. Under the revised provisions, the stock holding limit for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas and Assam have been fixed at two thousand quintals. The Ministry said, Kolkata sources sugar from Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka and supplies it to the eastern part of the country, including the North-Eastern region. The higher limit for Assam has been provided keeping in view geographical constraints, transportation logistics and consumer interest in the North-Eastern region. The Ministry said that average retail sugar prices have declined by 15 per cent from their August peak and are expected to decline further. Ex-mill sugar prices have also declined by approximately 28 per cent and have remained stable over the last three weeks. The decline reflects the impact of various measures taken by the Government to ensure adequate availability of sugar and facilitate its orderly movement through the market. Wholesalers and retailers have also been urged to immediately pass on the benefit of the substantial decline in ex-mill sugar prices to consumers.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 164 Defence Minister Rajnath Singh emphasises integrated financial systems for defence management and...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said that the same spirit of synergy and integration currently being emphasised among the three armed forces needs to be implemented within the financial framework of the Defence Accounts Department as well. Addressing the Defence Accounts Day in New Delhi today, he said that if the financial systems are also integrated, the entire defence management will become even more efficient. He said that this department serves as a common thread connecting the entire Ministry of Defence and is the backbone of the defence system. The Minister urged them to adopt and internalise the best practices in quality auditing at both the national and international levels and keep pace with evolving standards across the country and the world. Mr Singh stated that, during the last financial year, expenditure booking stood at approximately 100 percent. He said, this achievement marks a significant milestone and is a testament to the concerted efforts of the Defence Accounts Department and the three Services. The Minister added that this achievement reflects their unwavering commitment, dedication, hard work, and efficiency in ensuring the effective utilisation of resources. During the event, the Defence Minister launched several Information Technology initiatives of the Defence Accounts Department aimed at strengthening financial management and digital systems within the Ministry of Defence. These include the integration of the Indian Army Financial Information System with the Department’s SAKSHAM platform, the revamped National Compilation System for the Ministry of Defence, and the Payment Routing and Integrated System Management (PRISM) platform.

national_raw_news.title: Govt Officials, CRPF Personnel Join Cleanliness Drive Across Hyd - Deccan Chronicle
national_raw_news.content: Govt Officials, CRPF Personnel Join Cleanliness Drive Across Hyd Top Home South Andhra Pradesh Telangana Tamil Nadu Karnataka Keralam World NRI Nation Youth Entertainment Sholay Tollywood Bollywood Sandalwood Kollywood Mollywood Hollywood Movie Reviews Television Music Theatre OTT Sports Cricket Football Tennis Other News AI Videos Opinion and Editorials Business Enviroment Technology Youth Queer Beat Education Hyderabad Chronicle DC Decaf Featured Astroguide Home » Southern States » Telangana Govt Officials, CRPF Personnel Join Cleanliness Drive Across Hyd Telangana DC Correspondent 1 Oct 2026 9:18 PM IST 1 Oct 2026 9:18 PM IST PIB, CBC and CRPF officials joined cleanliness drives and plantation activities at multiple locations in Hyderabad as part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026. x PIB, CBC and CRPF officials and personnel participate in a cleanliness drive in Hyderabad. (Representational image: PTI) As Preferred Source Officials and staffers of the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) and Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) attended the cleanliness activities at different locations in Hyderabad on Thursday as part of the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign. The activities were held under the nationwide initiative — Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath — to promote cleanliness, civic responsibility and public participation. At the CGO Towers in Kavadiguda, PIB and CBC officials and staff members participated in a cleanliness drive and created awareness on maintaining clean surroundings. PIB Hyderabad additional director general Shruti Patil said cleanliness should not be treated as a one-day activity but as a daily responsibility. She emphasised public participation in the Swachh Bharat Mission and also urged officials and staff to make cleanliness part of their daily routine. She also appreciated the services of sanitation workers at the CGO Towers and distributed gloves and sanitation kits to them. Officials and staffers also participated in the saplings plantation at the CGO Towers under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative, aimed at increasing green cover and promoting environmental conservation. Separately, the CRPF Southern Sector organised an hour-long Shramdaan programme at Gopi Cheruvu, Serilingampally, from 8 am to 9 am. CRPF personnel, residents of Doyens Township and CMC staffers participated in cleanliness and sanitation activities around the lake. Serilingampally MLA Arekapudi Gandhi, CRPF inspector general Thummala Vikram, DIGs Praveen Ghag and others, along with CMC deputy commissioner Seva Islavath and other officials, participated in the programme. Residents and officials also encouraged tree plantation along the lake as part of efforts to maintain clean and healthy surroundings. national_raw_news.content: Tata Trust Vice Chairman Vijay Singh seeks inquiry into Tata Trusts’ governance, role in Tata Sons affairs Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Tata Trust Vice Chairman Vijay Singh seeks inquiry into Tata Trusts’ governance, role in Tata Sons affairs ANI | Updated: Oct 01, 2026 10:31 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 1 (ANI): Sir Dorabji Tata Trust trustee and Vice Chairman of the Trust Vijay Singh has sought an immediate inquiry by Maharashtra’s Charity Commissioner into the trust’s governance, alleging that its growing involvement in Tata Sons’ commercial affairs could jeopardise its charitable status and expose its assets to substantial tax liabilities. In an email dated September 25 addressed to the Charity Commissioner and the Deputy/Assistant Charity Commissioner for the Greater Mumbai region Singh, viewed by ANI, also sought scrutiny of trustee appointments and alleged interference with the independent decision-making of nominee directors on the Tata Sons board. Another trustee, Venu Srinivasan, has also written a similar letter to the Charity Commissioner, raising concerns over the trust’s governance and its involvement in Tata Sons’ affairs. “A matter of serious concern is the increasing involvement of SDTT and Tata Trusts in the commercial and strategic affairs of Tata Sons Private Limited,” Singh wrote. He argued that Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT), as a public charitable trust, should not assume the functions of a commercial enterprise or directly participate in running Tata Sons’ business merely because it holds a substantial shareholding in the company. Singh cited two Tata Trusts press releases dated September 17 concerning alternatives to listing Tata Sons and a proposal to provide liquidity to the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group. According to his email, the first release recorded that Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust had resolved in July 2025 that Tata Sons should remain unlisted and communicated that decision to the company. The second, he wrote, outlined a proposal placed by Tata Trusts Chairman Noel N. Tata before the Tata Sons board concerning monetisation of the SP Group’s shareholding. Singh said the proposal envisaged a buyout in two tranches, selective capital reduction through the National Company Law Tribunal and various financing sources. Singh alleged that these actions showed the trusts, through their chairman and operating team, taking a direct role in identifying, negotiating and seeking implementation of substantial commercial transactions involving Tata Sons. He warned that such involvement could put the trust’s income-tax registration and exemptions at risk, potentially affecting its charitable corpus. The email also challenged a circular resolution that Singh said SDTT circulated on September 16 to restrain Srinivasan, a nominee director jointly appointed by Sir Ratan Tata Trust and SDTT, from participating in or voting on the proposed listing of Tata Sons. Singh alleged that the move sought to prevent Srinivasan from exercising independent judgement and concentrate decision-making power within a smaller group of trustees. national_raw_news.title: KVIC Chairman hails Lijjat Papad women artisans, says organisation advances 'Vocal for ...
national_raw_news.content: KVIC Chairman hails Lijjat Papad women artisans, says organisation advances 'Vocal for Local' vision Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर KVIC Chairman hails Lijjat Papad women artisans, says organisation advances 'Vocal for Local' vision ANI | Updated: Oct 01, 2026 06:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 1 (ANI): Manoj Goyal, Chairman, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), addressed the women artisans of Shri Mahila Griha Udyog Lijjat Papad at an event held on Wednesday at the Sri Shanmukhananda Chandrasekharendra Saraswathi Auditorium in Sion (East), Mumbai. According to the MSME, as the chief guest, the KVIC Chairman applauded the work of the women artisans and highlighted the significant role played by organizations like Lijjat Papad in advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’. Addressing the congregation, Manoj Goyal opined that "the journey of Lijjat Papad, established on 15 March 1959 with just seven women and Rs. 80, was not merely an initiative to make Papads, but a dream of becoming self-reliant, living with dignity and standing on one's own feet. The recognition of Lijjat Papad as a Village Industry by KVIC in 1966 gave fresh momentum to this journey. Today, through its 83 branches across 16 states, more than 45,000 women are associated with Lijjat Papad and are progressing towards self-reliance and economic independence. Over the years, the organisation has diversified its product range. Besides papads, it also manufactures spices, flour, detergent and liquid soaps. Its products have reached more than 30 countries, including the USA, Australia, Japan and South Africa." KVIC Chairman said that the greatest strength of Lijjat Papad is its quality, hard work, and discipline. He said, “Lijjat does not merely make papads; it weaves together dignity, self-confidence, and opportunity.” Goyal said that Lijjat Papad’s achievements have also received national recognition. The organisation was honoured with the Best Village Industry Award in 2003, the Brand Equity Award in 2005 and the Women Development Award in 2017. Several international platforms and media organisations have also showcased Lijjat Papad’s inspiring journey to the world, the ministry said. Highlighting the activities and initiatives of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), the KVIC Chairman said that nearly 5 lakh artisans across the country are being provided employment, out of which 80% are women working in around 3,000 Khadi institutions. Over the past 12 years, the wages of Khadi artisans have increased by up to 275 per cent. He further stated that the production of the Khadi and Village Industries sector has increased to approximately ₹1.25 lakh crore, while sales have reached ₹1.87 lakh crore. Under the Village Industry Development Scheme, more than 3.23 lakh machines and toolkits have been distributed during the last 12 years. Similarly, under the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), around 11 lakh new projects have been established so far, with subsidies exceeding ₹30,000 crore, generating employment opportunities for approximately 1 crore people. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Press Information Bureau (PIB) Organises Swachhta Hi Seva 2026 Activities at National Media Centre Bureau Observes Swachhta Hi Seva 2026 with Tree Plantation, Collective Cleanliness Drive and Felicitation of Safai Mitras Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 4:39PM by PIB Delhi As part of the Swachhta Hi Seva 2026 campaign, a series of activities were organised at the National Media Centre (NMC), PIB Headquarters, focusing on environmental sustainability, cleanliness, sanitation and recognition of sanitation workers. A tree plantation drive was organised on September 30 under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative. The drive aimed to promote environmental sustainability and enhance green cover while encouraging collective participation in creating a cleaner and greener environment. It also highlighted the importance of nurturing trees and protecting the environment as a shared responsibility. Today, on October 1, a cleanliness drive was organised under the ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative. The drive focused on the cleanliness and upkeep of the NMC premises and encouraged officers and officials to contribute towards maintaining a clean and hygienic workplace. It also reinforced the importance of sanitation, hygiene and collective responsibility in furthering the objectives of Swachh Bharat. A felicitation ceremony for Safai Mitras/ Swachhagrahis/ Sanitation Workers was also organised today at the NMC. The ceremony recognised their dedicated efforts and valuable contributions towards maintaining cleanliness and sanitation at the workplace. The initiative highlighted the importance of acknowledging the role of sanitation workers and encouraging their continued contribution towards a cleaner and healthier environment. The activities were led by the Principal Director General, PIB, with the participation of officers and officials, reaffirming the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, cleanliness and a greener and healthier future.
